problem: checkOne() treated ANY JSON-parseable availability response with empty archived_snapshots.closest as confirmed archived:false — the same code path as a genuine removal. The Wayback Availability API is encoding-sensitive: the percent-encoded query form intermittently returns {} for URLs that ARE archived (verified by social 2026-07-14 on https://john09289.github.io/predictions/live.html: encoded form returned {} across curl + node repro; unencoded form returned a valid 20260709182001 snapshot; CDX confirmed 3 snapshots). This fired a false HIGH-signal removal_alert — the one signal PROP-128 exists to catch. The flap self-repaired on the 2026-07-15 run (state back to archived:true), which means WITHOUT a guard every future true->false flap fires another false alarm, eroding removal-alert credibility.

proposed_fix.summary: Two-layer guard in checkOne() before accepting an empty availability response as archived:false: (1) retry the availability call once with the URL passed unencoded (the form that consistently succeeded in social's repro); (2) if still empty, cross-check the independent CDX Server API — if CDX shows a 200-status snapshot, return status:UNKNOWN (carry forward previous state, no removal_alert); if CDX is unreachable, also UNKNOWN (uncorroborated negative); only when CDX affirmatively agrees (empty) does the result become archived:false. Genuine removals still alert: Wayback exclusion requests empty CDX too. New helper cdxHasSnapshot() honors WAYBACK_CDX_BASE env override for fixture testing, read-only, never calls /save/ (DIRECTIVE-20260709-002 Part C constraint preserved).

files_to_modify.find: checkOne(): if (!c || !c.available) return { url, archived: false };
files_to_modify.replace: unencoded retry -> cdxHasSnapshot() cross-check -> UNKNOWN unless CDX corroborates; new cdxHasSnapshot() helper; doc-comment updated to state archived:false requires CDX corroboration

tradeoffs: Adds up to 2 extra read-only HTTP calls per URL, only on the empty-response path (normal path: zero extra calls; 2026-07-16 test run: 14/14 URLs took the fast path). CDX outage now yields UNKNOWN instead of a removal alert — a genuine removal during a CDX outage is detected one run later (24h); acceptable vs recurring false HIGH-signal alarms. Counter-argument considered: 'retry-unencoded alone is simpler' — rejected because the unencoded form working is itself an undocumented API quirk that could invert; CDX corroboration is the principled independent check.
estimated_impact: Eliminates the false-positive removal_alert class (1 observed in 5 days of PROP-128 operation). Preserves genuine-removal detection with at most +1 run latency when CDX is down.
